ov: The largest bear and the largest land carnivore, living on Arctic sea ice and hunting seals. It’s classed as a marine mammal because it depends on the sea.

why.h: Only pregnant females den up for the winter, to give birth; other polar bears keep hunting on the ice.

rg: Arctic sea ice and coasts around the North Pole: Canada, Alaska, Greenland, Russia and Norway’s Svalbard.
df: Mostly seals, especially ringed seals, caught at breathing holes and at the ice edge.
fx: Its fur has no white pigment. It looks white because of the way light scatters off the hairs.
notes: ANSWER CHECK: animals.js says et:"no", but Wikipedia says polar bears have been hunted "for their coats, meat and other items", including by the Inuit. By how-we-answer's own rule ("In places: eaten in some countries or cultures, now or traditionally") this should probably be "some". why.h "only pregnant females": Wikipedia says mothers give birth in maternity dens; the "others keep hunting" half is standard but not quoted.
